videos.title: Civic Vocab 101: Gerrymandering
videos.description:
Fun fact: Colorado already took map drawing away from politicians. Since 2018, independent commissions draw our district lines, not the party in power.

So why does gerrymandering still matter here? Because the maps are only half the story. Even a fairly drawn district usually leans one way, which means the primary, not November, is where the real decision gets made. Fair lines don't fix who gets a real say in that primary.

videos.title: Election Hot Takes
videos.description:
Half of Colorado voters are unaffiliated. But our primaries still force them to pick a team before they can even vote.

Open Primaries fixes the mechanism: one ballot, every candidate, no party required.

This isn't about picking sides. It's about giving every voter the power they already deserve.

videos.title: Meet Alliance for Competitive Elections!
videos.description:
Meet our partners at the Alliance for Competitive Elections (ACE)! 

ACE is dedicated to making elections more competitive by training and uplifting minor party and independent candidates. 

Learn more at courageouscolorado.org.

videos.title: Do You Want More Choices in Politics?
videos.description:
If 80% of Coloradans want more choices in their politics, then we have to think differently about the system.

We need to be courageous enough to say where the system is not delivering. And courageous enough to provide solutions that may differ from our current setup.

If Coloradans aren't getting what they want, then we need to redesign the system — and put power back in the hands of voters.

videos.title: Meet Restore the Balance!
videos.description:
Meet Dave Murphy with Restore the Balance. 

Formed in the aftermath of January 6th, Restore the Balance is a nonprofit that brings people together across the political spectrum to reject extremism and rebuild good governance in Western Colorado.

Collaboration over division. Civility over chaos. This is what depolarization looks like on the ground.

Learn more at courageouscolorado.com.

videos.title: Should Colorado Primaries Reflect Our Unaffiliated Voters?
videos.description:
Colorado voters are changing. Should our primaries change with them?

Unaffiliated voters make up a major share of Colorado’s electorate. But when it comes to our primaries, they still have to choose between voting a Democratic or Republican ballot. They can’t vote across both.

That means a voter might prefer a Democrat for one office, a Republican for another, and an independent candidate somewhere else, but our current primary system doesn’t give them that flexibility.

Colorado voters aren’t neatly divided into two political camps.

Maybe our primary elections shouldn’t be either.

videos.title: What is a Fully Open Primary?
videos.description:
Your ballot shouldn’t come with a loyalty test.

A fully open primary gives voters the ability to choose between candidates, not parties.

Colorado’s current system gives unaffiliated voters more access than a fully closed primary, but they still have to choose one major party’s primary ballot rather than vote across party lines.

A fully open primary changes the question from “Which party’s ballot do you want?” to “Which candidates do you actually want?”

videos.description:
This September, the Denver Metro Activation Tour is bringing together residents, local leaders, students, and community organizations across Adams, Arapahoe, Boulder, Douglas, and Jefferson counties.

At each stop, we’re creating space to connect, hear what matters in your community, and explore practical ways to strengthen local democracy. Whether you’ve been part of Courageous Colorado from the beginning or you’re joining us for the first time, there’s a seat at the table for you.

📍 Find a tour stop near you and join the conversation. Link in bio for more information.

videos.title: Open Primaries: Who do you want on the ballot?
videos.description:
Open primaries answer one question: who do you want to see on the ballot?

Right now, most Colorado races are decided in the primary, not in November.

Closed and semi-closed primary systems keep that decision inside party lines, which
means unaffiliated and independent voters, who make up more than half the state,
don’t get a say in who is on the ballot come November.

An open primary makes elections competitive and fair. Every candidate, one ballot,
every voter. No party membership required to have a say.

videos.title: Term Limits: The Key to Fresh Voices in Government
videos.description:
Term limits create rotation. Rotation creates fresh voices.

The average member of Congress is significantly older than the average worker in
nearly any other profession. We're legislating on artificial intelligence, social media,
and the future of the energy economy and asking people who rarely, if ever, use
these tools daily to write the rules for them.
This is a structural flaw that needs to be changed.

videos.title: 50% of Coloradans Identify as Independent
videos.description:
People are tired of the major two-party system in our country and especially in
Colorado.

Luckily, with Colorado's semi-open primary system: unaffiliateds can still vote in the
primary election.

Now imagine taking that a step further where you're not choosing a party's ballot at
all. You're just voting for the candidate you actually believe in.

That's the kind of change that puts power back in voters' hands.

videos.title: We Ain't Leavin'!

#broncos #football

videos.title: Are Politics Broken?
videos.description:
Are politics broken or were they built this way?

We sat down with members of the Courageous Colorado Coalition to talk about the primary problem: partisan primaries, uncompetitive general elections, and a
semi-closed primary system that still shuts out too many voters.

videos.title: Are Open Primaries the Solve?
videos.description:
Dick Wadhams believes the open primaries would hold both parties, Democrat and
Republican, more accountable. Because in a closed primary, candidates only need
to appeal to their own party's base to win the primary and then the seat.

Open primaries change things: any voter, regardless of registration, can vote in either
primary. So a candidate now has to worry about appealing to unaffiliated and even
opposite-party voters to win, not just the base.

Cllaro is helping Latinos empower themselves through leadership development,
advocacy and research to strengthen Colorado.

Change happens in the community. We are working together to make a more open,
diverse, and better Colorado.

videos.title: What if politics could bring us together instead of driving us apart?
videos.description:
What if politics could bring us together instead of driving us apart? 

That’s what we’re working toward at Courageous Colorado: creating space for Coloradans from across the political spectrum to come together, have real conversations, and imagine a better way forward.

Because democracy works better when we listen, connect, and find common ground. 

Ready to join the conversation? Follow the link in bio.

videos.description:
Diversity in our elections? Politicians having to earn our vote? Not having to pick a
side?

You know what the answer is #openprimaries #openprimary #whatisanopenprimary

videos.title: Does Your Vote Matter in the Primary?
videos.description:
If you wonder if your vote matters in the primary election, well, it matters even more
than your vote in the general election.

Primary election turnout is low, often dramatically lower than the general. Fewer
voters means each individual vote carries more weight, not less.

Voting in a primary isn't just choosing a name. It's sending a signal to the candidates
and to the party about what you want representation to look like.

videos.title: What if Elections Rewarded Coalition Building?
videos.description:
What if elections rewarded coalition building among candidates? 

Our current elections are often full of division, with candidates attacking each other as they compete to win their party’s nomination. But, it doesn’t have to be this way. 

One possible solution is ranked choice voting (RCV). By allowing voters to rank candidates, RCV can encourage candidates to appeal beyond their core base and build broader coalitions, shifting the focus toward the issues that matter to voters, rather than personal attacks. 

Want to explore how we can improve our elections? Follow Courageous Colorado and su

videos.description:
Meet Colorado Common Cause, a member of the Courageous Coalition! 

Colorado Common Cause works to strengthen and protect our democracy by defending the right to vote, limiting the influence of big money in our elections, holding public officials accountable, and more.

Courageous Colorado is cross-partisan by design. We go beyond left versus right because this is about voter power, not party power.

If your organization wants to join the movement for a more open, representative, and responsive democracy, sign up through the link in our bio.

videos.title: What are Open Primaries?
videos.description:
Open primary vs. closed primary - what's the actual difference?

Closed primary: you can only vote for candidates in your own registered party. Registered Democrat? Democratic ballot only. No crossing over to a Republican or Green Party candidate. And if you're unaffiliated, your access depends entirely on your state and the party running the primary, sometimes you're in, often you're locked out.

Open primary: every voter picks which primary they vote in, regardless of registration. A registered Republican can vote on the Green Party ballot. A registered Democrat can vote for the Republican o

videos.title: Your Tax Dollars are Paying for the Primary Election
videos.description:
Coloradans, your tax dollars are paying for the primary election. Did you know that? Both parties' primary elections, actually.

So whether you’re participating or not, you are paying for it.

No taxation without representation is the reason this country exists. It is a fair question to ask of a system we all fund.
California, Washington, and Alaska do it differently. Every candidate on one ballot, every voter on the same ballot, no party lane to pick first.
That is possible here too.

❓DID YOU KNOW❓

videos.description:

Change starts here, subscribe to our newsletter to stay involved. Link in bio.

videos.title: Are Elections Rigged?
videos.description:
The system is rigged against solutions.

Saying elections are rigged undermines the democratic structure itself. What's actually happening is that the two parties benefit from how the system is built, and Americans don't.

Open primaries, campaign finance reform, election timing that gets more people voting.

Those are structural fixes, not partisan ones.
Subscribe to our newsletter to stay involved with Courageous Colorado.

Reform isn't left versus right. It's voter power, not party power.

videos.title: Get to Know Veterans for All Voters
videos.description:
Veterans for All Voters is one of the organizations in the Courageous Coalition.

They're a national network, veterans organized in all 50 states, advocating for reforms that lower the temperature in our politics and make government work better. 

Their model is local: show up in a community, find out what people are frustrated with, and back the veterans already working on it.

Courageous Colorado is cross-partisan by design. We go beyond left versus right, because this is about voter power, not party power. If your organization wants to be part of that, sign up through our link in bio.

videos.description:
Politicians shouldn't get to pick their voters before the voters get to pick them.

In Colorado, the primary is the decisive contest in a lot of races and it's the election almost nobody shows up for. The people with the most reason to be frustrated are the ones sitting it out.

That's fixable. It's a rules problem, not a people problem.

videos.title: The fight to widen who has a say didn't end in 1893.
videos.description:
The fight to widen who has a say didn't end in 1893. It's still going, and you're a part of it.

At Courageous Colorado, we believe every voter deserves a real say, no matter which party they choose or don't. When more people can take part on their own terms, our elections start to represent all of us.

videos.title: Election Changes Voters Agree On
videos.description:
Ask people across the political spectrum what would actually open up our democracy and you get a surprisingly consistent list.

All-candidate primaries, ranked choice voting, campaign finance change, election timing that brings more people in.

None of that is a partisan wish list. It is what voters and scholars across the spectrum keep landing on.

Colorado opened its primaries to unaffiliated voters in 2016. Turnout went up. We already proved change is possible here. At Courageous Colorado, we are working to keep opening it. Not because the system is broken beyond repair, but because we have

videos.title: Billionaires Benefit from Closed Political Systems
videos.description:
Ballot Measure 2 in Alaska would repeal three things: ranked choice voting, the open all-candidate primary, and the campaign finance disclosure laws voters passed in 2020.

Repeal them, and you eliminate the option for more voter power.
Repeal them, and the parties go back to deciding who's on your ballot before you ever see it.
Repeal them, and you remove the very law that lets you know when mega-donors like Elon Musk are putting millions of dollars behind changing how you vote.

The only way democracy evolves is if we're willing to change what's broken. Going back to the old system is a loss

videos.title: Elon Musk Attacks Vulnerable Red State
videos.description:
The only reason you know Elon Musk put $1.5M behind repealing Alaska's voting system is the exact campaign finance law that repeal would erase.

Ballot Measure 2 would undo three things Alaskans passed in 2020: the top-four open primary, ranked choice voting, and the disclosure rules that make donations like this public.

Alaska is the only state that pairs an all-candidate top-four primary with a ranked choice general. That structure changes who holds power in an election. It gives voters more names to pick from and shifts what candidates have to do to win.

videos.title: Who Gets the Final Say?
videos.description:
Understanding what ranked choice voting and open primaries are allows you to understand why Elon Musk donating $1.5 million to repeal Alaska's voting system is dangerous to our democracy.

In order to move forward, we need to elicit change in our voting systems, which Alaska did in 2020

Alaskans passed Ballot Measure 2 by about 3,700 votes. It bundled three changes:
1. Killed closed party primaries and replaced them with one primary ballot with every candidate on it, open to every voter. Top four advance.
2. Ranked choice voting in the general among those four.

videos.title: What do Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and some leaders of the Democratic party have in common?
videos.description:
If Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and some Democratic Party leaders all agree on something, it should cause some pause.

Right now in Alaska, millions are being spent to take away open primaries and ranked choice voting. The argument is always that it's confusing. The real reason is much simpler: open primaries take power out of party hands and place it back in the voters.


And parties don’t really want you to have that power.

videos.description:
Unite America's analysis shows nearly 90% of House races are already  decided by less than 10% of voters. 

In low-turnout closed primaries, more fringe candidates get elected, creating larger political pendulum swings.

Open primaries can create create more durable solutions that actually work.

#UniteAmerica #OpenPrimaries #primaryelection

videos.title: 2026 Primary Results (Nick Troiano): Least Competitive of Our Lifetimes
videos.description:
Fewer than 10% of voters effectively elected nearly 90% of Congress.

When closed primaries lock out 16.5M independents and leave over 150 House candidates running without real competition, voters lose.

Americans deserve competition, not coronation. Open primaries fix this. 🗳️

videos.title: Politicians Respond to Incentives
videos.description:
How do we change Congress? We need better ideas that alter the DNA of our incentive structure. 

When cooperation is punished and division is rewarded, politicians adapt to the system in front of them.

If our electoral system can be designed to reward division, it can also be redesigned to reward cooperation.

Glenn Nye tells us: better outcomes start with better incentives.

#UniteAmerica #OpenPrimaries #ElectionReform #VoterChoice #BetterGovernment

videos.title: Every Taxpaying Citizen Deserves a Ballot
videos.description:
"Simply leaving a political party should not disenfranchise me." 💡

Lisa Rice (CEO of Grow Democracy DC & Unite America Board Member) shares her story of joining the election reform movement and working towards solutions that enfranchise every voter. 

She led the charge in D.C. to pass and implement Initiative 83 - enfranchising independent voters across the District so all taxpayers get a vote.

In many states, millions of independent taxpaying Americans can’t participate in closed primaries every election cycle. It's time for common sense election reform. 

#Shorts #UniteAmerica #OpenPrimar

videos.title: Over Before November
videos.description:
In many states, the primary is the whole ballgame - with races effectively over before November. 

Nick Troiano joined @DecisionDeskHQOfficial with Chuck Todd and Chris Cilizza to discuss how states like Alaska are different - with the top 4 candidates moving on the general - creating real competition and more choice. 

In closed primary states, voters lose and parties win. Open primaries put power back where it belongs: with the voters. 🗳️

videos.title: Who Benefits from Closed Primaries?
videos.description:
Low-turnout primary elections benefit the fringes of the party. 

When the most extreme voices have more influence in our elections and which candidates move forward, there leaves little room for compromise in Washington. 

Opening primaries is a better reflection of democracy - giving all voters a voice and more choices at the ballot box. 

#UniteAmerica #OpenPrimaries #ClosedPrimaries #VoterChoice #ElectionReform

videos.title: Alaska's Better Way to Vote
videos.description:
Right now, Alaskans are walking into the voting booth - and doing something revolutionary.

Every voter, regardless of party, gets the exact same ballot. The top four candidates advance, and voters rank their choices in November. It's that simple.

And the results? Instead of politicians terrified of a primary challenge from their own party's fringes, Alaska elected leaders who actually govern. They’ve built cross-party coalitions to pass budgets, invest in infrastructure, and put their constituents first.

videos.title: Alaska Gets Things Done
videos.description:
How has changing to open, all-candidate primaries impacted Alaska? The results have been overwhelmingly positive. 

Since voters approved the open system in 2020, the number of voters casting a meaningful ballot has increased by nearly 60%.

Today, a cross-partisan governing majority is working on issues that matter to Alaskans - from passing the budget on time to funding education. 

When elected officials are accountable to more voters, they’re incentivized to do their jobs.

#Alaska #TopFourPrimary #VoterChoice #ElectionReform #VoterFreedom

videos.title: The Birthplace of American Democracy - Nick Troiano
videos.description:
Philadelphia’s Independence Hall is the birthplace of American democracy and the U.S. Constitution.

Yet today, Pennsylvania’s election system excludes nearly 1.4 million independent voters simply because they aren’t Democrats or Republicans.

That must change. To keep the republic strong for the next 250 years, everyone should be able to vote in every election and choose leaders who truly represent the people.

#UniteAmerica #IndependentVoters #Pennsylvania #America250

videos.description:

Well, that's exactly the way most of the country runs their elections with closed primaries. 

As districts have become so red or blue - and millions of independents are shut out of the process  - many voters can't participate in the election that ultimately determines the winner.

There is a better way: open, all-candidate primaries.

videos.title: Crowning Congress | Nick Troiano on C-SPAN
videos.description:
250 years after declaring independence from a monarchy, more than one-third of the U.S. House of Representatives is essentially handed power through "coronations." 

In this C-SPAN segment, Unite America’s Nick Troiano breaks down new data from the Unite America Institute: 150 House candidates in 2026 faced no meaningful competition, leaving 84.8 million voting-age Americans without a real choice at the ballot box.

videos.title: Closed Primaries vs. Open Primaries
videos.description:
If sports were like our primaries, many fans would get locked out before the game is even played. 
 
In 16 closed primary states, independent and unaffiliated voters can't participate. A complete fumble. 

Open primaries offer a different approach: one ballot, every candidate, every voter. No party gate. 

No separate entrance. Just a system where every voter gets the same ballot and all of the choices. 

#UniteAmerica #Preseason #Football #Politics #OpenPrimaries

videos.title: The Biggest Solvable Problem in Politics
videos.description:
Partisan primaries are not in the Constitution—they're a 100-year-old experiment that is no longer working for us. At Unite America, we are working to solve the primary problem by:

1) Letting every voter vote for any candidate, regardless of party affiliation.

2) Ensuring winners have true majority support, not just a plurality.

videos.title: What's Changed in Alaska?
videos.description:

It's simple. One ballot. Every candidate. All voters. 

This system gives the power back to the people. 

The stats show it: in Alaska, voter turnout in primaries is 37% compared to the national average of 21%. 

#Alaska #OpenPrimaries #IndependentVoters

#UniteAmerica #ColoradoVotes #COPolitics #COPrimary

For unaffiliated voters, casting a primary ballot isn't a partisan endorsement or a shift in personal ideology. 

Instead, it is a realization that true electoral influence happens where the definitive choices are made

#OpenPrimaries #MSNBC #PrimaryElection #Independents

videos.title: 40% of U.S. House Seats Already Decided
videos.description:
Shockingly, 40% of U.S. House seats have already been decided in low turnout party primaries. 

But, Nick Troiano of Unite America has some good news. Some states that voted Tuesday - like New Mexico and California - have open primary elections which give more voters a say.

For the first time, 380,000 independent voters were allowed to vote in New Mexico’s primary elections, boosting voter turnout in the state.

In California, all 26 million voters, more than 25% who are independent, were able to cast a ballot for any candidate - which increased the competitiveness of elections in the state.
